headline: UAE Work Visa 2026: Requirements, Costs and Process
metaDescription: UAE work visa 2026: employer-sponsored MOHRE permit, documents, fees, 6–10 week timeline, family sponsorship at AED 4,000/month and scam warnings explained.

sections.content:
A standard UAE work visa, also called an employment visa, lets a foreign worker live and work in the Emirates for a sponsoring employer. The employer, not the worker, drives the process: it must hold a valid trade licence and a clean compliance record with MOHRE or the relevant free zone authority, and the job role must match the company's licensed activities.

Applicants must generally be 18 or older, although older applicants can still get a permit case by case. There is no fixed minimum salary for a standard employment visa itself, which distinguishes it from self-sponsored routes such as the Green Visa, where skilled employees need a monthly salary of at least AED 15,000.
sections.title: How the Standard Employment Visa Works

sections.content:
Your employer will ask for a passport copy with at least six months' validity, a passport-sized photo, a signed offer letter and academic certificates for roles that require them. Regulated professions such as engineering and medicine need certificate attestation before the work permit is issued, and that step alone can add a week or more to the timeline, so it should start as early as possible.

After the work permit is approved, you enter the UAE on an entry permit, complete the mandatory medical fitness test and biometric appointment, and receive your Emirates ID. Health insurance is mandatory for every resident, and your employer must provide it or confirm your coverage before the residence visa is finalised.
sections.title: Documents and Step-by-Step Process

sections.content:
The cost breaks down into several government fees rather than one flat charge. At a typical free zone, a visa allocation fee runs around AED 1,600, the medical fitness test about AED 365, the establishment card around AED 640 and a change of status about AED 700, with mandatory health insurance from roughly AED 450 per month. Mainland employment adds its own MOHRE work permit fee on top.

Total costs therefore vary by emirate, free zone and package, and a standard licence bundled with one employment visa can start from around AED 14,290 at some free zones. Workers should confirm who pays each fee: legitimate employers normally cover recruitment and visa costs, and any demand for an up-front job fee is a red flag.

sections.content:
Skilled workers who want independence from a single employer can consider the five-year Green Visa, which requires a bachelor's degree, a MOHRE skill level 1, 2 or 3 role and a monthly salary of at least AED 15,000. Freelancers qualify with a freelance permit, a degree or specialised diploma and annual self-employment income of at least AED 360,000 over the previous two years.

Employees earning AED 4,000 a month or more can sponsor family members for residence, while the long-term Golden Visa targets higher earners at AED 30,000 a month, investors and recognised talents. From offer letter to landing, the standard employment route typically takes six to ten weeks, so applicants with attested documents ready can move fastest.
